verified: The 2026–2027 Dutch-language catalogue and February 2026 plan verify a 180 EC structure with a 75 EC Bèta-gamma core and 105 EC Earth Sciences major. Earth Sciences is first in the official major order. The mathematics example uses N&T (Mathematics B, selected as natural-science preparation) rather than counting both variants. Consultancy is the first of two Project 2 choices. The major includes 45 required EC and one 6 EC elective in year two, and 24 required EC and 30 EC of listed electives in year three. Scenario Planning fits in the final year-two block after the required Earth Sciences courses. Year three uses the five listed electives, one time each. The catalogue separately lists the 18 EC Future Earth bachelor project and 6 EC Research Designs. No additional unallocated minor credits are counted.
officialAlternative: Compared the dated programme tree and all selected course entries, the official study plan and published transition page, the archived Earth Sciences catalogue and the current Future Planet Studies project description. The dated transition page explicitly discontinues standalone Academic Skills and retains a resit for prior cohorts only. The new programming and cognition courses include skills assignments. Project 4 requires the old course by code, as well as Project 1, Project 3, first-year methods and philosophy, 48 first-year EC and 24 major EC. The latter thresholds fit the course sequence. No adopted replacement for the old skills condition was located. The Future Earth project’s entry text only addresses Future Planet Studies, while the related Research Designs course separately identifies a Bèta-gamma rule. The course’s membership and credits are verified, but the operative project entry rules for the 2026 Bèta-gamma cohort remain unconfirmed.
essentialEvidence: Confirm September 2026 Bèta-gamma entry rules for Project 4 and the Earth Sciences bachelor project. The Project 4 listing still requires the discontinued standalone Academic Skills course. The bachelor project lists Future Planet Studies prerequisites without a rule for Bèta-gamma students.
supportedComponents: One of two mathematics variants. This example uses the variant for students with Dutch pre-university Mathematics B.

allCatalogueUnits.name: Plant-Soil Interactions
allCatalogueUnits.entry: This course is open to students of the bachelor's programs Future Planet Studies and Bèta-gamma (major Earth Sciences). This course is also open to Exchange students and to students attending the minor Physical Geography, the minor Sustainable Food Systems and has limited access to elective students. Admission depends on previous education and availability but the applicant must at least have obtained 48 EC in first-year courses of his/her current program. Do take note that students with a background in social sciences must have successfully completed one semester (i.e. a study load of at least half of an academic year) in natural sciences courses related to Earth Sciences, Biology, Chemistry. Students with a background in one of these natural sciences are admitted to the course. This course is not open to first-year students.
allCatalogueUnits.recommendedPreparation: Soil science and chemistry knowledge as taught in ‘Toekomstperspectief voor de Aarde’ and ‘Energietransities’.

allCatalogueUnits.name: Desertification
allCatalogueUnits.entry: 48 EC first-year courses. For Future Planet Studies and Bèta-gamma (major Earth Sciences) students from cohort 2018-2019: The fieldwork of the course "Plant-Soil Interactions Practical" should have been passed (a pass for the partial grades for the fieldwork and a pass for the fieldwork report). The attendance requirements of the course "Digital Earth" must have been met. For Future Planet Studies and Bèta-gamma (major Earth Sciences) students from cohort 2017-2018 and before: participated in the fieldwork for “Soils & Environment” (a pass for the partial grades for the fieldwork and a pass for the fieldwork report) and attended the course “Digital Earth II”. No-resit opportunities for practical parts of the course. Components that have been assessed unsatisfactory can only be redone the following year. This course is part of the second year bachelor's program Future Planet Studies and Bèta-gamma (major Earth Sciences). The course is also open to students in the minor Global Water Challenge. Admission depends on previous education and availability. Do take note that students with a background in social sciences must have successfully completed one semester (i.e. a study load of at least half of an academic year) in natural sciences courses related to Earth Sciences, Environmental Sciences, Biology, Ecology or Climatology. Students with a background in one of these natural sciences are admitted to the course. This course is not open to first-year students, exchange students and elective students.
allCatalogueUnits.recommendedPreparation: The courses Plant-soil Interactions, as well as Digital Earth, should have been followed to be enrolled for this course! The report of the Plant-Soil Practical course should be passed!

allCatalogueUnits.name: Bachelorproject Future Planet Studies – Future Earth
allCatalogueUnits.entry: Completion of all first-year courses of Future Planet Studies. Having obtained at least 42 EC of the second year of Future Planet Studies. It is highly recommended to participate in the courses Research Designs, Bachelor Project Future Planet Studies, and Future Planet Project in one academic year.

allCatalogueUnits.name: Research Designs
allCatalogueUnits.entry: Future Planet Studies Completion of all first-year courses of Future Planet Studies. Having obtained at least 42 EC of the second year of Future Planet Studies. Bèta-gamma (major Earth Sciences) Completion of all first-year courses of Bèta-gamma. Exceptions will only be considered after consultation with the study advisor. It is highly recommended to participate in the courses Research Designs, Bachelor Project Future Planet Studies, and Future Planet Project in one academic year. This course is not open to elective or minor students.
allCatalogueUnits.recommendedPreparation: If students have not successfully completed the Quality of Life course yet, they are required to read the compulsory chapters of the book Research Methods (Walliman, 2011) before the start of Research Designs. The following chapters are mandatory: Research basics Structuring the research project The nature of data Collecting and analyzing secondary data Collecting primary data Quantitative data analysis Qualitative data analysis Writing the proposal AND writing up the research.
